title: Everest only wins on one ruler.
description:
Everest only wins on one ruler. It is the highest point above sea level, 8,848 metres. But height above the sea is one measurement of several, and it is the only one Everest tops.

Mauna Kea in Hawaii, measured from its base on the Pacific floor to its summit. That makes the Hawaiian volcano the tallest mountain on Earth, over a kilometre taller than Everest. Only about 4,205 metres of it stand above the water.

A third mountain wins, and it is the shortest. Earth bulges at the equator, so Ecuador's Chimborazo, sitting almost on it, pushes its peak 2,072 metres farther from the planet's core than Everest's while standing lower above the sea. NOAA calls it the closest point on Earth to the stars.

Highest, tallest, farthest out. Three mountains, three different rulers.

Sources:
- https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/highestpoint.html (NOAA National Ocean Service, National Geodetic Survey; read in full 26 Aug 2026): establishes that Mount Everest is the highest point above global mean sea level at 8,848 metres; that Mauna Kea in Hawaii is the tallest mountain from base to peak, rising more than 10,210 metres from the Pacific floor to its summit with only about 4,205 metres of it above the water; and that because Earth bulges at the equator from its rotation, the summit of Ecuador's Chimborazo, one degree south of the equator, sits over 2,072 metres farther from Earth's centre than Everest's summit even though Chimborazo is only 6,268 metres above sea level, which NOAA calls the closest point on Earth to the stars.
